question: What is the main focus of geriatrics?

options.A: The social and economic policies affecting retirement
options.B: The medical care and treatment of older adults
options.C: The cellular biology of genetic mutations in youth
options.D: The psychological development of children and teens

explanation: Spot on! Geriatrics is simply the branch of healthcare that focuses on keeping older adults healthy and treating age-related conditions. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is it risky to assume sudden confusion in an older adult is just 'normal aging'?

options.A: It automatically leads to permanent psychiatric institutionalization
options.B: It can cause nurses to miss acute illnesses like infections
options.C: It interferes with standard medication dosage calculations
options.D: It accelerates the natural hardening of the arteries

explanation: Great nursing insight! Never brush off sudden confusion as mere old age. It's often a red flag signaling a serious issue like a urinary tract infection or lack of oxygen. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h1)

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h2)

question: An elderly patient has a weakened cough reflex. What major complication are they at risk for?

options.A: Sudden enlargement of the vocal cords
options.D: Complete collapse of the nasal passages

explanation: Spot on! When older adults can't cough well, mucus stays trapped in the airways, becoming a breeding ground for bacteria and leading to chest infections. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why do older adults frequently struggle with constipation?

options.A: Overactive muscular contractions in the stomach
options.C: Slower peristalsis and reduced intestinal motility
options.D: Rapid absorption of water in the upper bowel

explanation: Exactly! As the gut ages, its muscle contractions slow down. This gives the body more time to absorb water from waste, leading to hard, difficult stools. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h3)

question: How does a slower kidney filtration rate affect drug safety in older adults?

options.A: It prevents oral medications from dissolving in the stomach
options.B: It forces all medications to be given through intravenous lines
options.C: It neutralizes the therapeutic effect of antibiotics instantly
options.D: It increases the risk of drug toxicity because drugs are cleared slower

explanation: Well reasoned! Since older kidneys filter blood more slowly, medications stay in the system longer and can build up to dangerous levels if doses aren't adjusted. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the medical term for the gradual loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?
explanation: Spot on! Sarcopenia is the natural, progressive shrinking of skeletal muscle that happens as we grow older. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a result of losing subcutaneous fat in old age?

options.A: Higher vulnerability to pressure injuries over bony areas
options.B: Increased ability to tolerate high summer temperatures
options.C: Impaired ability to maintain normal body warmth
options.D: Reduced natural cushioning against physical bumps

explanation: You nailed it! Losing that layer of fat actually makes it harder for older adults to handle extreme temperatures, rather than helping them tolerate summer heat. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the name for age-related hearing loss that usually starts with high-pitched sounds?
explanation: Correct! Presbycusis is the standard age-related hearing loss that typically makes high-frequency sounds harder to catch first. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h5)

question: An older patient complains that food tastes bland. Which age-related change causes this?

options.B: Rapid enlargement of the salivary glands
options.D: Decline in taste buds and olfactory nerve function

explanation: Spot on! Losing taste buds and having a weaker sense of smell dulls the flavor of food, which is why older adults often lose their appetite. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h5)

question: What term describes the natural, gradual decline of the immune system as people age?
explanation: You got it! Immunosenescence simply means the immune system gets a bit tired and weaker as we age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why might an elderly patient with a severe bacterial infection not run a high fever?

options.A: Older adults naturally maintain a much higher internal baseline temperature
options.B: The aging immune system has a blunted inflammatory and febrile response
options.C: Lung tissue infections never trigger body temperature changes at any age
options.D: Circulating white blood cells destroy all heat-producing chemicals instantly

explanation: Brilliant! Because of immunosenescence, older bodies often fail to mount a classic high fever, even when fighting a dangerous infection. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the golden rule of pharmacology when giving new medications to older adults?

options.A: Administer all drugs strictly on an empty stomach

explanation: Exactly! Always 'start low and go slow' with elderly patients to prevent nasty drug side effects since their bodies clear medications more slowly. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which assessment gives the best practical idea of an older adult's functional independence?

options.A: Checking only the laboratory values for liver and kidney function
options.B: Evaluating the patient's ability to perform activities of daily living
options.C: Measuring the exact circumference of the upper arm muscles
options.D: Reviewing the family medical tree for inherited genetic conditions

explanation: Spot on! Checking how well a patient handles activities of daily living (ADLs) tells you real-world details about how safely they can live on their own. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h7)
